Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

how many adjective

what number?

also as many as, how many?, how many of you

classical

Petr. 92.1: quot estis?
Ter. Ph. 454: Quot hominēs, tot sententiae

quot

indeclinable adjective

how many? as many as

Answered by tot: quot … tot, as many … so many.

Other words

  • quotus, quota, quotum — which in number? (what hour, how many in a party)

    adjective · also used · classical · Hor. S. 2.6.44: hōra quota est?; Mart. 14.218.1: dīc quotus … cupiās cēnāre

    “What time is it?” is hōra quota est?, which hour in the count (see “what time is it?”).

Examples

  • quot estis?

    how many of you are there?Petr. 92.1

  • quaeris, quot mihi bāsiātiōnēs tuae, Lesbia, sint satis superque

    you ask, Lesbia, how many of your kisses would be enough for me and more than enoughCatull. 7.1–2

  • Quot hominēs, tot sententiae; suus cuique mōs.

    So many men, so many opinions; each has his own way.Ter. Ph. 454

  • hōra quota est?

    what time is it?Hor. S. 2.6.44

  • dīc quotus et quantī cupiās cēnāre, nec ūnum addiderīs verbum: cēna parāta tibi est

    say how many you will be at dinner and what you want to spend, and don’t add a word: your dinner is readyMart. 14.218.1–2

See also how much, what time is it?.
